formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.WantedRecordOrder.label_injective {xs : List ℤ} {h J i i' j j' : ℕ}
    (hi : i < 3*xs.length) (hi' : i' < 3*xs.length)
    (hj : j < _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightGuardedWanted.totalKeys h J) (hj' : j' < _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightGuardedWanted.totalKeys h J)
    (he : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.WantedRecordOrder.label h J i j hi=_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.WantedRecordOrder.label h J i' j' hi') : i=i' ∧ j=j' := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $x$ be an integer list and let $i,i\prime<3|x|$ and $j,j\prime$ be below the complete global-key count for local parameters $h,J$. If the two physical index pairs decode to the same original wanted label, then $$i=i\prime\quad\text{and}\quad j=j\prime.$$

Transfers duplicate-freeness of physical pairs to distinct combinatorial labels. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
